learning_objective: 🎯 Calculate the perimeter and area of a full circle, and learn how to find the specific areas of pie-shaped sectors and chord-sliced segments!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The distance around the circle is Circumference (2πr). The space inside is the Area (πr²). Remember, π is approximately 22/7 or 3.14.
A sector is like a slice of pie formed by two radii. The formula to find its area is: (θ/360) × πr², where θ is the angle at the center.
An arc is a piece of the circumference. To find its length, use the formula: (θ/360) × 2πr.
A segment is the region bounded by a chord and an arc. To find the minor segment area: Find the Area of the Sector and SUBTRACT the Area of the Triangle formed by the radii and the chord.

fun_activity.title: 🍕 The Pizza Math
fun_activity.instructions: If you buy a 12-inch pizza and it's cut into 6 equal slices, what is the central angle (θ) of one slice? (Hint: A full circle is 360°, divide it by 6!). Now calculate the area of your 'Sector' slice!

exam_tips: 📌 Pay close attention to whether the question asks for the 'Minor' or 'Major' sector/segment. Major Area = Total Circle Area - Minor Area.
📌 To find the area of the triangle inside the sector, you will often need to use trigonometry (1/2 ab sin θ) or the equilateral triangle formula (√3/4 a²) if the central angle is 60°.
📌 Unless stated otherwise, always use π = 22/7 to make fraction cancellations easier.
quick_recap: ⭐ The angle subtended by a full circle at the center is 360°.
⭐ A semicircle is technically a sector with a central angle of 180°.
⭐ The length of the minute hand of a clock acts as the radius (r) when calculating areas swept over time.
